A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IET super-resolution work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary Sections F–H are readable and support comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original IET and IET-light reconstruction results, component and parameter ablations, attention visualizations, and inference-time measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original reconstruction experiments and reports additional ablations, token-similarity observations, and memory measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 changes the second-hop neighbor-selection schedule k2 from [12, 11, 9, 8] to [12, 10, 7, 6], altering the propagation budget. The core attention procedure, SF-FFN, losses, and model architecture remain unchanged; renaming expansion as propagation does not constitute another method change.

E1.justification: Coverage remains DF2K training for IET, DIV2K training for IET-light and ablations, and evaluation on Set5, Set14, BSD100, Urban100, and Manga109 for classical and lightweight SR at ×2, ×3, and ×4. The added analyses do not establish a new task or data domain.

E2.justification: The external benchmark comparators and the appendix's ATD, IPG, and PFT runtime comparators are unchanged. However, Table 1 revises the internal comparison variants: DLSG-centered combinations are replaced by propagation/sparsification/SF-FFN combinations, including sparsification-only and explicitly SF-FFN-disabled controls.

E3.justification: v2 describes Table 1's baseline as fixed dilated attention, whereas v1 specifies local attention with d=1. It adds neighbor-ratio and SF-FFN configuration sweeps, extends the depth sweep to one step, removes the inference-dilation-5 case, and adds memory as an evaluation measure. These are reported protocol changes within retained tasks; the PDFs do not establish which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 substantially expands component validation: Table 1 is redesigned, depth ablations gain FLOPs and an additional setting, and new Tables 4–6 test k1/k2 ratios, SF-FFN placement, and fused-neighbor counts. New Figure 2 examines global-attention neighbor overlap. These additions investigate previously untested design choices, especially SF-FFN, while most existing visual analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial ablation and memory results and replaces several component/depth entries. Benchmark updates are small: classical ×2 Urban100 PSNR changes from 35.07 to 35.09, Manga109 from 40.61 to 40.60, and lightweight ×2 Urban100 from 34.00 to 34.03. These are revised reported results, not established same-configuration gains. Appendix runtimes remain unchanged, while Table 9 adds memory values but retains older ×2 IET PSNR values inconsistent with Table 7.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 newly states the asymptotic attention-cost comparison O(N²) versus O(kN). This is a limited addition to mathematical cost characterization; Equations (1)–(8), the candidate-selection definitions, and the expander-graph initialization argument remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: individualized asymmetric candidate selection, efficient global dependency modeling, and state-of-the-art SR performance under comparable computational budgets. Updated numerical margins and supporting analyses do not redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: v2 more explicitly attributes the main gains to propagation and sparsification's main benefit to computational savings. It adds explanations linking late SF-FFN placement to more reliable similarities and additional fused neighbors to redundancy. Appendix G newly acknowledges higher memory use than ATD/IPG and explains the lower usage relative to PFT.

D1.justification: v2 revises the documented neighbor-count schedule, adds tensor dimensions to architecture diagrams, and documents preferred SF-FFN placement in the final two blocks through ablations. These additions do not establish a previously different SF-FFN implementation. Appendix training recipes, GPU information, and the code-link target were already present and remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 48 referenced works are retained after matching renumbered entries. A new sparse-attention paragraph explicitly contrasts IEA with spatial-window SwinIR, dilated-window ART, hash-based NLSA, and clustering-based ATD, providing a limited expansion of research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 renames expansion as propagation, replaces DLSG terminology with dilation-based initialization, rewrites parts of the motivation and ablation discussion, adds related-work subheadings, reorders the depth/dilation discussion, and condenses the conclusion. Much of the abstract, introduction, method description, and supplementary training text remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively converted from two-column to single-column layout. Figure 1 gains attention-matrix illustrations, the former initialization Figure 2 is replaced by a similarity analysis, Figure 3 is redrawn, and Figures 4–5 gain dimensional annotations. Ablation tables are added and restructured, and the appendix runtime table gains memory and PSNR columns. Existing reconstruction images are retained and resized.

improvement.justification: The added SF-FFN and propagation ablations, FLOPs comparisons, and memory measurements make design choices and efficiency tradeoffs better supported than in v1. The gain is limited by unresolved experimental-setting ambiguities and a new reporting inconsistency: v2 Table 9 retains ×2 IET PSNR values of 35.07/40.61 while Table 7 reports 35.09/40.60. Overall, the additional diagnostic evidence improves the paper modestly despite these shortcomings.
